Whereas last year 33,060 children were abused and neglected in Michigan totaling 91 children, each day, and whereas it is estimated that in 2019 63 of Michigan's children died from child abuse and neglect. Whereas unemployment, poverty, parental drug and alcohol abuse, stress, social isolation and violent communities are identified risk factors for child maltreatment. While statewide and nationally child abuse is considered to be one of our nation's most serious public health problems and scientific studies documenting the link between abuse and neglect of children to a wide range of medical, emotional, psychological, and behavioral disorders, such as depression, alcoholism, drug abuse, severe obesity and juvenile delinquency. Whereas prevention strengthens families and is cost effective and research shows that spending for child abuse prevention programs save dollars that would be spent for crisis oriented programming, such as protective services, foster care, special education, and And whereas child abuse prevention is an acknowledged community responsibility and on behalf of Michigan's children. This month, and each month thereafter, we join the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services and the Children's Trust Fund to commit to always and always remember the power of one. This statewide initiative, under the leadership of the Children's Trust Fund, asserts the power of one person, one community, one dollar, one action during April to help protect children from abuse and neglect throughout Michigan. Now, therefore, the Madison Heights City Council does hereby proclaim April of 2020 as Child Abuse Prevention Month in the city of Madison Heights.
